disease_mutation_row.name: disease_mutation_row
disease_mutation_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid AS doid
FROM disease_mutation dm
disease_mutation_row.description: Row-level view exposing disease_mutation rows and all raw columns needed for filtering, projection, and joins. Intended as the base cohort of individual mutations.
validated_on: Show me all information about disease mutations with amino acid residue (ref_aa) equal to E

disease_mutation_with_tissue.name: disease_mutation_with_tissue
disease_mutation_with_tissue.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dmt.uberon_anatomical_id
FROM
  disease_mutation AS dm
JOIN
  disease_mutation_tissue AS dmt
  ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_with_tissue.description: Denormalized mutation rows joined to any mapped tissue/uberon anatomical id from disease_mutation_tissue. Useful for filtering or grouping mutations by anatomical site.

mutation_transcript_uniprot_map.name: mutation_transcript_uniprot_map
mutation_transcript_uniprot_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  mpdm.peptide_id AS peptide_id,
  mpdm.uniprotkb_ac AS uniprotkb_ac,
  muc.uniprotkb_canonical_ac AS uniprotkb_canonical_ac
FROM
  disease_mutation AS dm
  LEFT JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation AS mpdm
    ON dm.ensembl_transcript_id = mpdm.ensembl_transcript_id
  LEFT JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id AS muc
    ON mpdm.uniprotkb_ac = muc.uniprotkb_ac
mutation_transcript_uniprot_map.description: Mapping of disease mutations to protein/UniProt identifiers using ensembl_transcript_id -> map_protein_disease_mutation and canonical UniProt where available. Useful when analyses require UniProt-level grouping or enrichment.

fda_tests_rowlevel.name: fda_tests_rowlevel
fda_tests_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  test_manufacturer,
  -- normalized manufacturer: lowercased and trimmed for simple normalization
  lower(trim(test_manufacturer)) AS test_manufacturer_normalized,
  test_approval_status,
  -- boolean flag whether manufacturer is null or all-whitespace
  (test_manufacturer IS NULL OR trim(test_manufacturer) = '') AS test_manufacturer_is_null
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test
fda_tests_rowlevel.description: One row per FDA test as recorded in biomarker_fda_test. Exposes identity columns and common descriptive/filterable attributes for cohorting and counting.
validated_on: How many FDA tests did manufacturer 23andMe?

fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.name: fda_test_manufacturer_normalized
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  test_manufacturer,
  -- Lifted literals for normalization rules:
  -- 1) trim whitespace and reduce internal whitespace to single space
  -- 2) lower-case
  -- 3) remove common company suffixes (inc, llc, ltd, co, corp, corporation, incorporated, company)
  -- 4) remove punctuation like .,/-()
  -- The example implementation performs these steps using regexp_replace and lower().
  (
    -- step 1 & 2: normalize whitespace and lowercase
    regexp_replace(
      lower(regexp_replace(coalesce(test_manufacturer, ''), '\s+', ' ', 'g')),
      -- step 3 & 4: remove punctuation and common corp suffixes (word boundaries)
      '\b(\.|\,|\/|\-|\(|\))\b', '', 'g'
    )
  ) AS test_manufacturer_normalized
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.description: Normalized manufacturer names for FDA tests to support case/whitespace-insensitive matching and simple canonicalization.

fda_tests_by_manufacturer_counts.name: fda_tests_by_manufacturer_counts
fda_tests_by_manufacturer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- original manufacturer string as present in the FDA test table
  t.test_manufacturer                                  AS test_manufacturer,
  -- normalized manufacturer name (lifted out as a literal from source rows;
  -- normalization logic should be done before this view if needed)
  t.test_manufacturer_normalized                       AS test_manufacturer_normalized,
  -- count distinct tests by their unique submission identifier to avoid double-counting
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.test_submission)                    AS num_tests
FROM
  -- source: row-level FDA tests view which provides manufacturer fields and test_submission
  fda_tests_rowlevel AS t
WHERE
  -- exclude rows with no manufacturer information when counting by manufacturer;
  -- if you want to include NULL manufacturers as a bucket, remove this filter.
  NOT t.test_manufacturer_is_null
GROUP BY
  t.test_manufacturer,
  t.test_manufacturer_normalized
fda_tests_by_manufacturer_counts.description: Counts of FDA tests aggregated by manufacturer. Useful to answer 'how many tests does manufacturer X have' and to get top manufacturers by test count.

species_by_genus.name: species_by_genus
species_by_genus.body_sql:
SELECT
  species.speciesid AS speciesid,
  species.speciescommonname AS speciescommonname,
  species.genus AS genus
FROM
  species
WHERE
  -- liftable filter literal: only include rows matching this genus (set literal below)
  (genus = 'Homo' OR 'Homo' IS NULL)
species_by_genus.description: Cohort of species rows with genus and common name exposed for filtering and projection.

normalized_species_names.name: normalized_species_names
normalized_species_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  speciesid,
  /* Lifted literals: none required; normalization uses standard functions */
  -- normalize speciescommonname: trim and lower-case; collapse internal whitespace to single space
  regexp_replace(lower(trim(speciescommonname)), '\s+', ' ', 'g') AS speciescommonname
FROM species
normalized_species_names.description: Species rows with cleaned/canonicalized common name and genus (trimmed and lowercased) to support text-matching and consistent presentation.

species_base.name: species_base
species_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  speciesid,
  genus,
  species,
  speciescommonname
FROM
  species
species_base.description: Normalized projection of the species table exposing stable id and taxonomic name fields. Use for any question that needs species rows, joins to species, or ordering by id or name.
validated_on: Show me all information about species

disease_mutation_row_level.name: disease_mutation_row_level
disease_mutation_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id::bigint AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos::bigint AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos::bigint AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos::bigint AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb::bigint AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq::bigint AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid::bigint AS doid
FROM disease_mutation dm
disease_mutation_row_level.description: Normalized, row-level projection of the disease_mutation table exposing all mutation attributes needed for downstream queries and joins. Performs no aggregation; casts/normalizes columns as-is so consumers can filter/group by raw mutation fields.
validated_on: Show all information about disease mutations
counter_examples: Show disease mutation chromosome positions for skin cancer
List all disease mutation chromosome positions data for disease skin cancer

disease_mutation_with_articles.name: disease_mutation_with_articles
disease_mutation_with_articles.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid
FROM disease_mutation AS dm
JOIN disease_mutation_article AS dma
  ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_with_articles.description: Denormalized view linking disease mutations to supporting article PMIDs. One row per (disease_mutation.id, pmid) — useful for filtering or counting mutations with literature support.

disease_mutation_tissue_mapping.name: disease_mutation_tissue_mapping
disease_mutation_tissue_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  dmt.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM disease_mutation AS dm
JOIN disease_mutation_tissue AS dmt
  ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_tissue_mapping.description: Mapping of disease mutations to uberon anatomical IDs (tissues) where the mutation is observed. One row per (disease_mutation.id, disease_mutation_tissue.uberon_anatomical_id). Useful for filtering mutations by tissue or linking to anatomical metadata.

biomarker_row_level.name: biomarker_row_level
biomarker_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_row_level.description: One canonical row per biomarker exposing identity and descriptive fields; nulls preserved so callers can filter out missing descriptions or other fields. Useful as the base row-level cohort for queries about biomarkers and their attributes.
validated_on: Show me the gene symbol of biomarkers

biomarker_aliases_expanded.name: biomarker_aliases_expanded
biomarker_aliases_expanded.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.aash AS id,
  ba.alias AS alias
FROM (
  -- Lifted literal: none (keeps schema-driven)
  -- Biomarker base rows: carry primary id through as biomarker_internal_id -> alias join key
  SELECT
    biomarker.id AS aash
  FROM
    biomarker
) b
JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.aash
biomarker_aliases_expanded.description: Denormalized rows of biomarker identifiers joined to their aliases. One row per (biomarker.id, alias). Useful for searches by alias or to present alternate names alongside canonical biomarker rows.

biomarker_articles.name: biomarker_articles
biomarker_articles.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  ba.pmid AS pmid
FROM
  biomarker b
JOIN
  biomarker_article ba
    ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_articles.description: Mapping of biomarkers to literature (PMID). One row per (biomarker.id, pmid). Useful to connect descriptive text to publications and to restrict biomarkers to those with literature evidence.

fda_tests_rowlevel_15.name: fda_tests_rowlevel_15
fda_tests_rowlevel_15.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.test_trade_name,

  t.test_manufacturer,

  t.biomarker_origin
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test AS t
fda_tests_rowlevel_15.description: Normalized row-level view of FDA tests exposing test identity, manufacturer, and submission fields. Keeps one row per test_trade_name + test_submission (the natural key in biomarker_fda_test).

fda_test_trials_rowlevel.name: fda_test_trials_rowlevel
fda_test_trials_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM

fda_test_trials_rowlevel.description: Row-level mapping of FDA tests to individual trial identifiers. One row per trial (test_trade_name, test_submission, test_trial_id).

fda_test_with_trials_join.name: fda_test_with_trials_join
fda_test_with_trials_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.test_trade_name,
  t.test_submission,
  tt.test_trial_id,
  t.test_manufacturer,

  ON tt.test_trade_name = t.test_trade_name

fda_test_with_trials_join.description: Denormalized view joining FDA tests to their trials. One row per trial with test metadata included for filtering and grouping.

biomarker_row.name: biomarker_row
biomarker_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel,
  b.id AS id
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_row.description: Base row-level biomarker records exposing primary identifiers, gene symbol, description, and panel flag. One row per biomarker.
counter_examples: Show the gene symbol and the description of cancer biomarkers which are not in a panel

biomarker_aliases.name: biomarker_aliases
biomarker_aliases.description: Denormalized mapping of biomarker rows to their aliases. One row per biomarker alias (biomarker_internal_id + alias). Useful to expand searches to include alternate names.
validated_on: Show me the gene symbol of biomarkers
counter_examples: Show me the description of all biomarkers
Show the gene symbol and the description of cancer biomarkers which are not in a panel

biomarker_extra_identifiers.name: biomarker_extra_identifiers
biomarker_extra_identifiers.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  ba.pmid AS pmid,
  be.id AS biomarker_edrn_id,
  bf.id AS biomarker_fda_id
FROM biomarker b
-- articles: zero or more pmids per biomarker (biomarker_article.biomerker_internal_id -> biomarker.id)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
-- EDRN entries: zero or more (biomarker_edrn.uberon_anatomical_id not used here)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn be
  ON be.id = b.id
-- FDA biomarker mapping table (biomarker_fda.id) may reference biomarker.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda bf
  ON bf.id = b.id
biomarker_extra_identifiers.description: Additional identifiers and external links for biomarkers (articles, EDRN, FDA entries) joined to the biomarker row. One row per biomarker id per external identifier to allow filtering by presence/absence of external links.

disease_row.name: disease_row
disease_row.body_sql:

FROM

disease_row.description: Normalized disease rows exposing canonical id and name; suitable as the base row-level cohort for disease filters and projections.

biomarker_basic_lookup.name: biomarker_basic_lookup
biomarker_basic_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  be.biomarker_title AS biomarker_title_edrn,
  be.qa_state AS qa_state_edrn,
  be.phase AS phase_edrn,
  -- alias: prefer a single concatenated string of aliases for the biomarker id (lift literal: alias separator)
  string_agg(ba.alias, ', ' ORDER BY ba.alias) FILTER (WHERE ba.alias IS NOT NULL) AS alias
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn be
  ON be.id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
GROUP BY
  b.id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  be.biomarker_title,
  be.qa_state,
  be.phase
biomarker_basic_lookup.description: Denormalized biomarker identity map joining EDRN biomarker id to general biomarker table and aliases for lookup and display.

biomarker_edrn_core.name: biomarker_edrn_core
biomarker_edrn_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  biomarker_title,
  qa_state,
  biomarker_type,
  uberon_anatomical_id,
  phase
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_core.description: Canonical projection of biomarker EDRN records with key identifying columns and commonly queried attributes (title, state, type, phase and anatomical linkage). Normalizes column names and exposes raw values for downstream filtering and joins.
validated_on: Show me the title of biomarkers on the EDRN platform with biomarker type different from Protein.
counter_examples: Show me all biomarkers on the EDRN platform with type protein in phase two.

biomarker_basic_identity.name: biomarker_basic_identity
biomarker_basic_identity.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id
FROM
  biomarker b
biomarker_basic_identity.description: Basic identity and primary identifiers for biomarkers from the biomarker table, useful to join EDRN records to broader biomarker metadata (gene symbol, whether test is a panel, biomarker_id).

biomarker_gene_canonical.name: biomarker_gene_canonical
biomarker_gene_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  NULLIF(trim(b.gene_symbol), '') AS gene_symbol_clean
FROM
  biomarker b
biomarker_gene_canonical.description: Normalized projection of biomarker gene symbols: trims NULLs and canonicalizes empty/blank to NULL. Exposes one row per biomarker.id with the cleaned gene_symbol to support distinct-list and join operations.

biomarker_to_fda_test_join.name: biomarker_to_fda_test_join
biomarker_to_fda_test_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  t.test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  t.test_submission AS test_submission,
  t.test_manufacturer AS test_manufacturer,
  t.platform_method AS platform_method,
  t.test_approval_status AS test_approval_status
FROM biomarker b
JOIN biomarker_fda bf ON bf.id = b.id
JOIN biomarker_fda_test t ON t.test_trade_name = bf.test_trade_name AND t.test_submission = bf.test_submission
biomarker_to_fda_test_join.description: Denormalized join between biomarker and FDA test records where available. One row per biomarker.id per matching FDA test (trade name + submission). Useful for questions combining biomarker genes with test-level metadata (manufacturer, platform, approval status).

biomarker_canonical.name: biomarker_canonical
biomarker_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS "biomarker.id",
  b.gene_symbol AS "biomarker.gene_symbol",
  b.biomarker_id AS "biomarker.biomarker_id",
  ba.alias AS alias,
  bac.pmid AS pmid,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
-- left join aliases: zero, one, or many aliases per biomarker
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
-- left join articles / pmids: zero, one, or many pmids per biomarker
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article bac
  ON bac.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_canonical.description: Canonical biomarker identity rows linking biomarker main id to other biomarker tables (biomarker, biomarker_alias, biomarker_article). Useful to find cross-references, aliases, and literature pmids for a biomarker id.

anatomical_entity_lookup.name: anatomical_entity_lookup
anatomical_entity_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  anatomical_entity.id                                             AS "anatomical_entity.id",
  anatomical_entity.name                                           AS "anatomical_entity.name",
  anatomical_entity.description                                    AS "anatomical_entity.description"
FROM
  anatomical_entity
anatomical_entity_lookup.description: Normalized lookup of anatomical entities (uberon ids) to human-readable names and descriptions. Useful for translating uberon_anatomical_id referenced by other tables.

biomarker_with_anatomical_context.name: biomarker_with_anatomical_context
biomarker_with_anatomical_context.body_sql:
SELECT
  biomarker_edrn.id                                    AS "biomarker_edrn.id",
  biomarker_edrn.biomarker_title                       AS "biomarker_edrn.biomarker_title",
  biomarker_edrn.biomarker_type                        AS "biomarker_edrn.biomarker_type",
  biomarker_edrn.uberon_anatomical_id                  AS "biomarker_edrn.uberon_anatomical_id",
  anatomical_entity.id                                 AS "anatomical_entity.id",
  anatomical_entity.name                               AS "anatomical_entity.name",
  anatomical_entity.description                        AS "anatomical_entity.description"
FROM
  biomarker_edrn
LEFT JOIN
  anatomical_entity
ON
  biomarker_edrn.uberon_anatomical_id = anatomical_entity.id
biomarker_with_anatomical_context.description: Biomarker EDRN records joined to anatomical_entity via uberon id to provide human-readable anatomical name and description alongside biomarker metadata.

differential_expression_rows.name: differential_expression_rows
differential_expression_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  de.log2fc AS log2fc,
  de.pvalue AS pvalue,
  de.adjpvalue AS adjpvalue,
  de.expression_change_direction AS expression_change_direction,
  de.statistical_significance AS statistical_significance,
  de.subjects_total AS subjects_total
FROM
  differential_expression de
differential_expression_rows.description: Row-level differential expression records for genes measured in specific diseases (by disease ontology id). One row per differential_expression record (a measured gene x disease pair).
validated_on: Get the p-value of differential expressions for the disease 'lung cancer'
Return gen symbol and pvalue for the expression of gene with symbol 'EGFR' in lung cancer
Show name of diseases where the gene expression with symbol A1BG has a statistical significance of 'Yes'

healthy_expression_by_anatomy.name: healthy_expression_by_anatomy
healthy_expression_by_anatomy.body_sql:
SELECT
  ensembl_gene_id,
  uberon_anatomical_id,
  uberon_developmental_id,
  expression_level_gene_relative,
  expression_level_anatomical_relative,
  expression_score,
  expression_rank_score
FROM healthy_expression
healthy_expression_by_anatomy.description: Row-level healthy tissue expression measurements for genes across anatomical terms. One row per ensembl_gene_id x uberon_anatomical_id x uberon_developmental_id measurement.

xref_ensembl_to_symbol.name: xref_ensembl_to_symbol
xref_ensembl_to_symbol.body_sql:
SELECT
  x.ensembl_gene_id AS ensembl_gene_id,
  x.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  x.speciesid AS speciesid
FROM xref_gene_ensembl AS x
WHERE x.ensembl_gene_id IS NOT NULL
  AND x.ensembl_gene_id <> ''
xref_ensembl_to_symbol.description: Normalized mapping of Ensembl gene IDs to HGNC gene_symbol for genes in this database (one row per ensembl_gene_id).

biomarker_core.name: biomarker_core
biomarker_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_core.description: Canonical biomarker rows with key identifiers and cleaned text fields; one row per biomarker.id.

biomarker_aliases_and_articles.name: biomarker_aliases_and_articles
biomarker_aliases_and_articles.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  ba.alias AS alias,
  ba2.pmid AS pmid
FROM biomarker b
-- aliases (may be zero..n)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
-- articles (may be zero..n) : biomarker_article links biomarker_internal_id -> pmid
-- use a separate alias (ba2) to allow Cartesian between aliases and pmids when both exist
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article ba2
  ON ba2.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_aliases_and_articles.description: Denormalized associations of biomarker ids to their aliases and linked article PMIDs; one row per (biomarker.id, alias, pmid) combination to enable text-matching or provenance filtering.

biomarker_edrn_phase_values.name: biomarker_edrn_phase_values
biomarker_edrn_phase_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  trim(phase) AS phase
FROM
  biomarker_edrn
WHERE
  phase IS NOT NULL
biomarker_edrn_phase_values.description: Normalized projection of the phase values recorded for EDRN biomarkers, cleaned to exclude NULLs and trimmed. One row per biomarker_edrn record (preserves original id) exposing the raw phase string for downstream distinct/aggregation.

biomarker_edrn_phase_canonical.name: biomarker_edrn_phase_canonical
biomarker_edrn_phase_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  -- lift literal transformations out: canonicalization is trim(lower(phase))
  CASE
    WHEN phase IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(lower(phase))
  END AS canonical_phase
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_phase_canonical.description: Canonicalized phases for EDRN biomarkers: projects biomarker_edrn.id and a trimmed/lowercased canonical_phase to normalize variant spellings/case. Keeps one row per biomarker_edrn record so callers can aggregate or deduplicate as needed.

fda_test_row.name: fda_test_row

  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  -- mapped UniProt accession from the transcript->peptide map (may be null when no mapping)
  m.uniprotkb_ac AS uniprotkb_ac,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,

FROM

  disease_mutation_row dm
LEFT JOIN

  mutation_transcript_uniprot_map m
ON
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id = m.ensembl_transcript_id
disease_mutation_with_transcript_map.description: Denormalized mutation rows joined to transcript/protein mapping (Uniprot/peptide) to provide canonical protein identifiers alongside mutation fields for downstream joins and filtering.

fda_test_manufacturer_normalized_47.name: fda_test_manufacturer_normalized_47
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized_47.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  -- canonical manufacturer string: trimmed, lowercased, common punctuation normalized,
  -- collapse consecutive whitespace, and map empty -> NULL. Lifted literals: the set of
  -- characters to replace and the replacement are expressed in SQL functions below.
  NULLIF(
    regexp_replace(
      lower(
        regexp_replace(
          trim(coalesce(test_manufacturer, '')),
          '[' || regexp_replace('.,;:/\&()[]{}<>\"''\t\n\r', E'\\\\', 'g') || ']+',
          ' ',
          'g'
        )
      ),
      '\s+',
      ' ',
      'g'
    ),
    ''
  ) AS test_manufacturer_canonical,
  test_manufacturer
FROM biomarker_fda_test
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized_47.description: Normalized/cleaned view of biomarker_fda_test with trimmed/canonicalized manufacturer string and preserved primary keys and other useful columns for grouping and filtering.

GROUP BY

fda_test_counts_by_manufacturer.description: Pre-aggregated counts of FDA test rows grouped by normalized manufacturer. Useful for quickly answering counts per manufacturer and top manufacturers by test count.

differential_expression_cleaned.name: differential_expression_cleaned
differential_expression_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  -- numeric columns: pass through as-is (already numeric types in schema)
  de.log2fc::double precision AS log2fc,
  de.pvalue::double precision AS pvalue,
  de.adjpvalue::double precision AS adjpvalue,
  -- cleaned statistical_significance: trim and normalize empty -> NULL, preserve case as-is but remove surrounding whitespace
  NULLIF(trim(de.statistical_significance), '') AS statistical_significance,
  -- normalized expression_change_direction:
  -- canonicalize common textual variants into one of: 'up', 'down', 'no_change', NULL
  CASE
    WHEN de.expression_change_direction IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction))
  END AS _ecd_norm_raw,
  -- final expression_change_direction mapping (carry through gene/doid by selecting from computed raw)
  CASE
    WHEN de.expression_change_direction IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction)) IN ('up', 'increased', 'increased expression', 'upregulated', 'up-regulated', 'up regulated', 'positive') THEN 'up'
    WHEN lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction)) IN ('down', 'decreased', 'decreased expression', 'downregulated', 'down-regulated', 'down regulated', 'negative') THEN 'down'
    WHEN lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction)) IN ('no_change', 'no change', 'unchanged', 'stable', 'none', 'nochange', 'no_change_detected') THEN 'no_change'
    WHEN lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction)) IN ('mixed', 'both', 'varied') THEN 'no_change'
    WHEN lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction)) ~ '^(up|down)[\\s\\-]?regulat' THEN
      CASE WHEN lower(trim(de.expression_change_direction)) LIKE 'up%' THEN 'up' ELSE 'down' END
    ELSE NULL
  END AS expression_change_direction
FROM differential_expression de
differential_expression_cleaned.description: Normalized differential expression rows with canonicalized expression change direction, numeric significance measures, and trimmed/cleaned text columns. One row per differential_expression record (gene_symbol + doid).
counter_examples: Show the pvalue of differential expression of lung cancer

differential_expression_upregulated_coho.name: differential_expression_upregulated_cohort
differential_expression_upregulated_coho.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol,
  de.doid,
  de.log2fc,
  de.pvalue,
  de.adjpvalue,
  de.statistical_significance,
  de.expression_change_direction
FROM
  differential_expression de
WHERE
  -- lift literals: up-regulated direction keywords and significance threshold
  (
    lower(de.expression_change_direction) = 'up'
    OR lower(de.expression_change_direction) = 'upregulated'
    OR lower(de.expression_change_direction) = 'up-regulated'
    OR lower(de.expression_change_direction) = 'increased'
  )
  AND (
    -- significance: prefer adjusted p-value if present, otherwise raw pvalue
    (de.adjpvalue IS NOT NULL AND de.adjpvalue <= 0.05)
    OR (de.adjpvalue IS NULL AND de.pvalue IS NOT NULL AND de.pvalue <= 0.05)
  )
differential_expression_upregulated_coho.description: Subset (cohort) of differential_expression rows flagged as up-regulated (case-insensitive variants) and that meet a significance criterion. One row per differential_expression record (gene_symbol + doid). This view is a reusable cohort for questions about up-regulated genes in diseases.

gene_identity_normalized.name: gene_identity_normalized
gene_identity_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  coalesce(xg.gene_symbol, dg.gene_symbol) AS gene_symbol,
  coalesce(xg.ensembl_gene_id, dg.ensembl_gene_id) AS ensembl_gene_id,
  xg.speciesid AS speciesid
FROM
  (
    /* All distinct gene_symbol <-> ensembl_gene_id pairs known from xref_gene_ensembl */
    SELECT
      gene_symbol,
      ensembl_gene_id,
      speciesid
    FROM xref_gene_ensembl
    WHERE ensembl_gene_id IS NOT NULL
  ) xg
FULL JOIN
  (
    /* Fallback: derive gene_symbol from other tables that use gene_symbol but lack xref.
       Lifted literals: none */
    SELECT DISTINCT
      gene_symbol,
      NULL::character varying AS ensembl_gene_id
    FROM (
      SELECT gene_symbol FROM biomarker WHERE gene_symbol IS NOT NULL
      UNION
      SELECT gene_symbol FROM differential_expression WHERE gene_symbol IS NOT NULL
    ) s
  ) dg
ON xg.gene_symbol = dg.gene_symbol
WHERE coalesce(xg.gene_symbol, dg.gene_symbol) IS NOT NULL
gene_identity_normalized.description: Canonical mapping between gene symbol and ensembl gene id and species context (if available via xref). Useful to normalize gene identifiers across tables.

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; preserve all joined rows

biomarker_basic_lookup_73.description: Denormalized lookup of biomarkers combining biomarker (primary metadata) with biomarker_edrn (EDRN-specific metadata) by biomarker id. Exposes biomarker.id, biomarker.gene_symbol and biomarker_edrn.phase so queries can filter or group phases alongside biomarker identifiers.

disease_with_differential_expression.name: disease_with_differential_expression
disease_with_differential_expression.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.id AS id,
  d.name AS name,
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.pvalue AS pvalue
FROM
  disease d
JOIN
  differential_expression de
    ON de.doid = d.id
disease_with_differential_expression.description: Denormalized join of disease rows to differential expression results, one row per (disease.id, gene_symbol) where differential_expression.doid = disease.id. Useful for filtering differential expression by disease name or DOID.
